One ticket, one delegator, one PR. Branch and worktree already exist and already carry the intake commit: /Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee-worktrees/mrq-133-agent-evaluator, branch mrq-133-agent-evaluator off github/main @ 8dc17d3.

READ FIRST, in order:
  (1) sequence/agent-evaluator-design.md — THE BINDING DESIGN. Every ruling, invariant, and UI placement is settled there; this description is the summary, that file is the contract.
  (2) EVALUATION.md section 2.5 (AC-288 – AC-293) and sequence/USER_STORIES.md Amendment 20 (US-87) — already minted on your branch. Write tests to satisfy them. Do NOT edit them and do NOT mint more ACs (COMMON.md: delegators never edit contract docs).
  (3) src/lib/reviewer-scope.ts in full — the load-bearing file, and the only uncontended one.
  (4) DESIGN.md (Flight Deck; chip vocabulary) and CLAUDE.md "Rules of the road".
  (5) PHILOSOPHY.md section on agent-native design — this ticket is that principle taken literally.

WHAT THIS IS. Marquee ships no built-in AI reviewer. It ships the seat an external agent sits in: the organizer's own model, own prompt, own rubric, on the organizer's own credential. An agent evaluator is a person row with kind='agent' holding a reviewer membership and track scopes — assigned through the control that already assigns reviewers, counted in the coverage that already counts reviewers, badged everywhere a reviewer name renders. THERE IS NO PARALLEL AI SUBSYSTEM. If you find yourself writing `if (isAgent)` inside the evaluation write handler, the design has been lost; re-read section 4 of the design doc.

WHY IT DOES NOT WORK TODAY, precisely. Two independent failures. (a) SKILL.md has no review surface at all — its registry is seed/triage/chase/agenda/publish/diagnose, so an agent reading it learns it may bulk-accept but may not record reasoning. (b) reviewer-scope.ts's reviewerPersonIdForEvent returns null for any non-session principal, so authorizeReviewerScope 403s every bearer token on the reviewer record and evaluation-write routes. That function's own comment names service integrations as the anticipated future and states the exact precondition: tokens "do not identify a reviewer person". This ticket SUPPLIES THE IDENTITY. It does not weaken a single authorization check.

SCOPE, in build order (each numbered block is a shippable stage):

1. Migration — people.kind ('human'|'agent', default 'human', CHECK) and api_tokens.acts_as_person_id (nullable FK to people) with a partial index. TAKE THE NEXT GENUINELY FREE MIGRATION NUMBER after checking merged main at the moment you write it — main is at 0007, and four open PRs add 0008–0010 including two different 0009s. Do not assume 0011. Name it distinctively: NNNN_agent_evaluator_seats.sql.

2. Identity resolution — auth-middleware.ts resolves a token carrying acts_as_person_id AS that person (load the seat's memberships, expose actingPersonId); reviewerPersonIdForEvent accepts session.personId OR token.actingPersonId and runs every existing check unchanged against it. Rewrite that function's doc comment to describe the world as it then is — no "previously" narration (house rule: write timelessly).

3. Security invariants, section 4.3 of the design — six of them, each needing its own test. The two that carry the feature: a token may act ONLY as a kind='agent' person, checked at issue AND re-checked at resolution so a row edited under a live token fails closed; and a bound token acts only as the seat, never additionally as the issuing human, with its named scopes constrained to review:write at issue. Treat any simplification of these as out of bounds.

4. Seat creation — "Add agent evaluator" on the /evaluation committee card, beside the human invite. Name + track responsibilities, one transactional API call producing person + reviewer membership + reviewer_track_scopes + committee_members + bound review:write token, secret returned once and rendered through the EXISTING shown-once panel pattern (ApiTokensPage.tsx:195 — reuse the component, do not build a second secret UI).

5. The badge — a neutral "Agent" Chip everywhere reviewer_name renders: SubmissionRecordPage.tsx:165 (the evaluation-evidence line) and :168 (the Evaluation panel assignment rows and the Assign reviewer select). Reserve its width so a row never reflows between a human and an agent reviewer (CLAUDE.md: elements never jump). Add it to the chair results table ONLY if MRQ-109 has landed on your base; if it has not, build against what exists and say so in the PR body.

6. Rulings to implement, not relitigate — agent scores are EXCLUDED from the human aggregate and rendered as their own labelled line (R1); agent completions DO count toward assignment coverage (R2); Marquee never invokes a model — no cron, no queue consumer, no run-the-agent button (R3); one seat per agent, not per run (R4); the word is "Agent", never "AI", in user-facing strings (R5).

7. CLI + SKILL.md — `review queue`, `review show`, `review submit` matching the existing registry shape and --json discipline; a Review section in SKILL.md placed between Triage and Chase, carrying a worked loop (read queue, read record, post score with rationale), regenerated through cli/generate-skill.mjs. tests/node/skill.AC-142-144.test.mjs gates the content byte-for-byte — read it before writing.

8. Seed, and it is NOT optional — reset-demo must produce a "Triage agent" seat, a real evaluation from it on "Taming 40-Minute CI" whose comment is specific to that abstract (CI duration, monorepo, build caching — not boilerplate reusable on any submission), and at least one HUMAN review on the same submission so the distinction is visible side by side with no setup.

THE ONE TRAP (design doc section 9, and AC-293 enforces it). The eval kit's ABS-14 is judged only if the product claims AI review anywhere in its UI or marketing; nothing does today, so it is scored not-applicable and excluded. The moment the "evaluation is open" claim ships, ABS-14 becomes graded and demands an agent score with substantive rationale on that exact seeded submission, agent-vs-human distinguishable, and a human override persisting across reload. SHIP THE CLAIM AND THE EVIDENCE IN THE SAME PR OR SHIP NEITHER.

COLLISIONS. MRQ-107/108/109/110 are all open PRs on this exact surface (review.routes.ts, evaluation.routes.ts, EvaluationPage.tsx, SubmissionRecordPage.tsx). Base on github/main; rebase and re-run the gate whenever one lands; npm ci after every rebase (COMMON.md). reviewer-scope.ts is yours and uncontended.

OUT OF SCOPE. Marquee-hosted inference of any kind. Prompt storage, rubric templates, or model configuration in-product — the prompt is the operator's asset and lives with them. Agent seats for any role but reviewer. Comparison-mode agent participation. Retro-badging historical seed reviews beyond the one worked example.

DONE MEANS: npm run pr-gate green, AC-288–293 covered by tests you can point at, a PR open against Stage-11-Agentics/marquee base main, and a completion comment naming any deviate-with-flag calls you made.
data.title: Evaluation is an open seat — agent evaluator identity, badge, skill, and seeded evidence

data.body: Plan committed and pushed at c6339e3. Refreshed base github/main @ 72648d6; MRQ-109 chair results surface is present; migration number will be rechecked immediately before creation. Validation scope recorded: local c11 browser + CLI only, no external domains or real credentials.
Plan refresh 38cbccbd pushed after rebasing onto github/main @ 97e0920. npm ci passed post-rebase; schema/auth implementation begins against that exact base.

Self-review PASS at 85cb2f2b. Reviewed auth-middleware bound-seat resolution and reviewer-scope invariants; generic token binding is strict/rejected, live kind is re-checked, issuer memberships are not carried into bound tokens, and existing track/assignment helpers remain authoritative. Reviewed aggregate SQL: human-only headline/criterion/recommendation results, separate agent_reviews evidence, and all-reviewer coverage. Reviewed UI: one shared TokenSecretPanel, fixed-width ReviewerName Agent slot, assignment picker chip, record evidence and chair results lines, settings seat label. AC trace passes with AC-288 through AC-293 covered. No contract docs edited. Refreshed-base schema mirror repair is flagged for PR.

Validation PASS at 85cb2f2b. Ran npx vite dev on http://127.0.0.1:8805 with local D1 migrations and seed; used the UI reset-demo flow and re-authenticated. Created Live CLI evaluator in Evaluation, selected all eight track scopes, observed its Agent badge, assigned it through the existing Initial review record picker to sub_synthetic-pool-0002 (Taming 40-Minute CI), and confirmed the picker showed a reserved Agent badge. The real CLI review queue returned that assignment; review submit wrote score 4.7, recommendation maybe, and substantive monorepo/build-cache rationale. Reloaded the chair record and saw the live Agent row beside the human row; a chair Accept override persisted across reload. Reset demo again and re-opened the seeded record with Triage agent 4.50 rationale plus human 4.20 review and badges without setup. Server stopped after proof; temporary HTTP cookie setting restored.
